export_rights.summary: Per the Cloud Data Processing Addendum (which covers Google Workspace), Google will enable the customer, during the term and in a manner consistent with the functionality of the services, to access, rectify, restrict processing of, and export customer data. The customer may instruct return of data during the term and retains a recovery window after the term ends before deletion.
export_rights.post_termination_window: Up to 30 days after end of term (CDPA 'recovery period'); after that, Google deletes remaining customer data within a maximum of 180 days unless law requires storage.

routes.how: Google Vault API (vault.googleapis.com): POST /v1/matters to create a matter, POST /v1/matters/{matterId}/exports (matters.exports.create) with a query plus ExportOptions per service; poll matters.exports.get until status COMPLETED; export files land in a Google-managed Cloud Storage bucket (cloudStorageSink.files gives bucketName/objectName) and are downloaded via the Cloud Storage JSON or XML API. OAuth 2.0 with scope https://www.googleapis.com/auth/ediscovery.
requires: Google Vault privileges and access to the matter (creator, shared, or View All Matters privilege)
gotchas: Export names containing special characters (~!$'(),;@:/?) can prevent the export from being downloaded (per Vault API schema docs)
Gmail confidential-mode content is only included when MailExportOptions.showConfidentialModeContent=true
Drive files linked from Gmail messages are only included when MailExportOptions.exportLinkedDriveFiles=true
Drive access-level metadata for indirect-access users requires DriveExportOptions.includeAccessInfo=true
Vault edition/SKU availability requirements could not be confirmed from reachable docs

routes.how: Gmail API (gmail.googleapis.com): GET /gmail/v1/users/{userId}/messages (users.messages.list, paginated) then GET /gmail/v1/users/{userId}/messages/{id}?format=raw (users.messages.get) to retrieve each message as full RFC 822 content; labels, threads, and drafts have parallel list/get resources. OAuth 2.0 bearer token with https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.readonly scope.
requires: OAuth 2.0 token with https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.readonly scope, authorized for each target mailbox
gotchas: users.messages.list returns at most 500 messages per page (default 100); paginate via nextPageToken
format=raw returns the message base64url-encoded inside a JSON envelope; decode to get the .eml content
Org-wide (other users') mailbox access requires admin-side authorization; the mechanism (domain-wide delegation) is not documented in the sources consulted

routes.how: Google Drive API v3 (https://www.googleapis.com/drive/v3/): GET /files (files.list, paginated) to enumerate, GET /files/{fileId} with alt=media to download binary content, GET /files/{fileId}/export?mimeType=... (files.export) to convert Google-native documents (Docs/Sheets/Slides) to standard formats; the About resource's exportFormats map lists supported source-to-target MIME conversions. OAuth 2.0 with https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.readonly or drive scope.
formats: exported MIME types per about.exportFormats map
requires: OAuth 2.0 token with https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.readonly (or broader drive) scope, authorized for each target user or shared drive
gotchas: files.export content is limited to 10 MB per exported file (per API reference); larger Google-native docs need another route (e.g. Vault Drive export)
Google-native files (Docs/Sheets/Slides) have no binary content to download directly; they must be exported/converted
Shared drive items require supportsAllDrives=true on requests or they may be missing

routes.how: Admin SDK Directory API (admin.googleapis.com): GET /admin/directory/v1/users (users.list, paginated, per domain or customer), GET /admin/directory/v1/groups (groups.list), GET /admin/directory/v1/groups/{groupKey}/members (members.list); parallel resources exist for org units, role management, aliases, and mobile devices. OAuth 2.0 with the relevant admin.directory.*.readonly scopes.
requires: Google Workspace admin credentials/authorization for Admin SDK
OAuth 2.0 token with admin.directory.* readonly scopes (e.g. admin.directory.user.readonly, admin.directory.group.readonly)
gotchas: users.list and groups.list are paginated; iterate nextPageToken
members.list times out after 60 minutes on very large groups (per API reference)

routes.how: Admin SDK Reports API (admin.googleapis.com): GET /admin/reports/v1/activity/users/{userKey}/applications/{applicationName} (activities.list) with applicationName from a documented enum (admin, login, drive, gmail, token, groups, calendar, chat, meet, vault, saml, chrome, and others); filter with startTime/endTime (RFC 3339), paginate with nextPageToken. Usage data via customerUsageReports.get / userUsageReport.get / entityUsageReports.get. OAuth 2.0 with https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.reports.audit.readonly (and admin.reports.usage.readonly for usage).
requires: Google Workspace admin authorization for Admin SDK Reports
OAuth 2.0 token with admin.reports.audit.readonly / admin.reports.usage.readonly scopes
gotchas: maxResults is capped at 1000 activity records per page
For the gmail application, startTime and endTime are mandatory and may span at most 30 days per request
Overall audit-log retention periods are documented on support.google.com, which was not consulted — verify retention in-tenant before relying on this route for history

routes.how: Google Calendar API v3 (https://www.googleapis.com/calendar/v3/): GET /users/me/calendarList (calendarList.list) to enumerate calendars, then GET /calendars/{calendarId}/events (events.list, paginated) per calendar; acl.list exposes per-calendar sharing. OAuth 2.0 with calendar.readonly-class scopes.
requires: OAuth 2.0 token with Calendar API read scopes, authorized per user
gotchas: API returns JSON event resources, not ICS; Vault's Calendar export and end-user Takeout are the documented ICS-producing routes (Takeout docs not consulted)

preservation_notes.attachments: Drive files bulk-extract via Drive API files.list + files.get (alt=media); Google-native docs must go through files.export, which is limited to 10 MB per file. Gmail attachments come out inside raw RFC 822 messages (Gmail API format=raw) or via Vault Gmail exports (MBOX/PST), with linked Drive files optionally included via exportLinkedDriveFiles.
preservation_notes.audit_log: Exportable as JSON via Admin SDK Reports API activities.list per application (admin, login, drive, gmail, token, etc.), paginated at 1000 records/page; gmail activity queries limited to 30-day windows. Documented retention periods live on support.google.com, which was not consulted — retention unconfirmed.
preservation_notes.config_artifacts: Org structure (users, groups, members, org units, roles, aliases) is readable as JSON via the Admin SDK Directory API, but no restorable whole-tenant export of Admin console settings/policies was documented in the sources consulted.

notes: Several well-known routes are deliberately omitted rather than described from memory because their documentation was not consulted: the Admin console Data Export tool ('Takeout for organizations', support.google.com/a/answer/100458), end-user Google Takeout (MBOX/ICS/HTML archives), Google Chat/Groups UI exports, and any edition/SKU gating (e.g. which editions include Vault). API quota/rate-limit pages were not consulted, so all rate_limits are null — quotas exist and must be checked before bulk extraction. The Admin SDK Data Transfer API (admin.googleapis.com/admin/datatransfer/v1/transfers) transfers Drive/Calendar ownership between users at offboarding; it moves data rather than exporting it, so it is not listed as a route.
research_caveats: The research environment's egress proxy blocked support.google.com, developers.google.com, workspace.google.com, and other Google doc hosts; only cloud.google.com and googleapis.com (API Discovery Service) were reachable, and the web-search budget was exhausted. The Admin console Data Export tool, end-user Takeout, Chat/Groups UI exports, edition/SKU gating, API quota pages, domain-wide delegation, and audit-log retention periods are therefore omitted or unconfirmed rather than described from memory.
